incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike observed for customer PineGate (single-tenant). 10m p99 jumped from 240ms -> 3.4s. Automated mitigation engaged: scaled routing to dedicated fallback pool. Trace: https://redwood.internal/trace/3923456789

maya: I see the alert, paging oncall. @liam you oncall?

liam: Oncall here. Looking at console now. PineGate's sessions show lots of streaming stalls and long tails. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 3.4s per the dashboard.

sophia: Adding context: they rolled an experimental prompt generator last night that creates very long repeated prefixes for each request (avg prefix tokens ~ 1200). Might be related to long KV cache churn.

devon: Confirmed. I grep'd logs: many requests with prompt_type=oddball-generator and sequence_length > 1000. Also seeing repeated KV cache misses and recurrent cold starts.

maya: Can you paste the relevant logs?

devon: ```
2026-03-15T18:33:12Z pine-req-9876 INFO seq_len=1248 kv_miss=true cache_pop=9 latency_ms=3120
2026-03-15T18:33:13Z pine-req-9877 INFO seq_len=1302 kv_miss=true cache_pop=12 latency_ms=2890
2026-03-15T18:33:14Z pine-req-9878 INFO seq_len=1156 kv_miss=true concurrency=24 latency_ms=3450
```

zara: Interesting — concurrency spikes correlated with these long prefixes. Their client has aggressive concurrency; we see per-session multiplexing up to 40 concurrent streams.

liam: Current mitigations in place: routing to fallback pool + temporary rate limit on single-tenant bursts (throttle 20reqs/s). That reduced p99 to ~1.2s but still above SLO.

sophia: Could this be KV cache eviction thrash because prefix keys are huge and unique per request? If cache is getting churned, streaming would stall waiting for KV loads.

devon: Agreed. Also the runtime shows elevated memory pressure on the serving nodes because of long context. Kernel selector is falling back to slower path for long sequences.

maya: Immediate action proposals (short list):
1) Keep fallback routing + maintain throttle at 20rps.
2) Temporarily enable prefix deduplication on PineGate's route (hash-based prefix truncation to 512 tokens) if allowed.
3) Ask PineGate to reduce concurrency or batch their requests.

liam: I can enable prefix truncation on the route as a soft override flag. Need PRD approval? Ops has emergency toggle. @ops-bot can you confirm toggle availability?

ops-bot: Emergency toggle available: route_override.prefix_truncate=512. Will apply with 30s cooldown. Confirm to proceed.

maya: Proceed. Apply now.

ops-bot: Applied route_override.prefix_truncate=512 to customer PineGate at 18:36:22 UTC.

liam: Observing metrics... p99 dropped from ~1.2s -> 460ms over next minute. p95 back near baseline (~260ms). Streaming stalls decreased significantly.

sophia: Nice. We should still investigate root cause: why client sent such long unique prefixes. Probably a bug or experiment. We need to notify customer and recommend best practices.

devon: I'll capture a perf profile and KV cache hit/miss rates for the last 2 hours and attach to the incident ticket.

zara: Also recommend adding a hard guard in routing that rejects requests with prefix > 2000 tokens for single-tenant routes by default.

maya: Good idea. For now, let's keep throttles and prefix truncation until PineGate acknowledges. I'll open a support ticket and ping their engineering contact.

liam: Handing off to daytime oncall @zara in 15 minutes. Will leave notes in the incident ticket and include mitigation TTL (keep truncation for 24h unless customer requests rollback).

zara: Got it. I'll monitor and escalate to eng-runtime if we see any regression.

maya: Post-mortem action items so far:
- (devon) collect perf traces + KV metrics (ETA 2h)
- (sophia) add safeguard rule proposal for long-prefix single-tenant flows (ETA 48h)
- (liam) draft customer communication + mitigation note (ETA 30m)
- (zara) monitor and validate rollback plan (ongoing)

liam: Drafted message to customer: "We detected a pattern of unusually long and unique prefixes that caused cache churn and tail latency increases. We've applied a temporary server-side prefix truncation to keep latency within your SLO while we investigate. Please review and consider reducing prefix length or batching." Will send after Maya approves.

maya: Please send and request they confirm changes to their generator. Also ask them to run a short load test with reduced concurrency.
